column3: The Hebrew names his seed in the singular; BSB says descendants.
The Hebrew’s three adjectives are singular without an explicit second for; BSB introduces the gracious, compassionate, and righteous as recipients.
The Hebrew makes the man actively order his affairs in justice without an explicit freely; BSB says affairs are guided and lends freely.
The Hebrew simply says he will look on his foes without explicit triumph; BSB supplies in triumph.
The Hebrew says he scattered and gave without explicitly naming gifts; BSB supplies his gifts.
The Hebrew has a singular desire of the wicked; BSB has desires.
